rationale: Both reviews are deep, well-evidenced, and largely non-overlapping with each other, but X lands squarely on the single most important confirmed ground-truth finding — hsliuustc0106's High-severity report that legacy MOSS-Audio-Tokenizer checkpoints silently mis-instantiate as v2 because both configs share model_type and from_pretrained doesn't reject the mismatch — reproducing the exact mechanism almost verbatim. Y's review covers the same code region but lands on a different, less central issue (overly-broad except masking real v2 errors), missing the actual reported bug. Both independently catch the WER-fallback-bytes issue (linyueqian's comment) and the NPU seq_token_counts gap, and both are highly actionable with file/line citations; Y's explicit validation passes and ready-to-apply suggestion blocks give it a slight edge in precision/actionability, but X's recall advantage on the headline ground-truth bug is decisive enough for a narrow overall win. Neither includes a labeled LATENT GAP CHECK section.
